unlisted_practices: Extend WHO Prequalification to AI-as-a-medical-device only through reform, rather than transposing the pharmaceutical prequalification model unchanged.

Require the national regulatory authority of the deploying country to meet a defined standard, including post-market safety surveillance infrastructure for AI medical devices, before relying on WHO prequalification of an AI tool.
Allow AI manufacturers to engage WHO proactively to determine the appropriate prequalification pathway rather than waiting for WHO to solicit products.
Have WHO assess AI medical device manufacturers' compliance with core harmonised standards such as ISO 13485, IEC 62304 and ISO 42001.
Establish confidential master-file submission and independent WHO audit of generative AI foundation model dossiers, including training data and development documentation.
Issue WHO digital certificates linked to a model's cryptographic hash or version ID so countries can confirm they hold the certified generative AI version and only run local bridging studies.
Require local clinical evaluation of effectiveness in each country's population, with oversight devolved to national regulatory authorities.
Use predetermined change control plans to manage AI model drift and updates for regulated AI medical devices.
Use current model evaluation science, such as recent sample size methods for external validation, when setting validation requirements for AI tools.
